html:
ForgeMCP Latest Development Updates

Date: October 30, 2026 Development status: Active development; acceptance is specific to each evidence gate.

October 30, 2026 — Hand finger-flexion correction applied; playback gate pending

The correction execution report records the confirmed cause: positive local-X flexion keys on the four finger chains bent away from the palm. Those keys were reversed on a versioned copy, v003; the 22-bone rig and normalized weights were preserved, and the v002 baseline was restored to its original bytes. Independent Blender readback and sampled evaluated poses cover each finger, the thumb, combined curl, a stronger closed pose, open and neutral return. Continuous timeline playback could not be verified because the UI control pipe was unavailable. The anatomical correction milestone is partially complete, not production accepted; webcam tracking remains proposed future work.

October 30, 2026 — Hand rigging, automatic skinning and animation prototype

The hand-rigging milestone records the saved and reopened Blender 5.2.3 artifact: a 22-bone custom hand hierarchy, native automatic weights on all 9,584 vertices, five isolated digit-motion checks and the Hand_Demo_Animation Action. The delivered v002 file is not an Auto-Rig Pro rig; its automatic weight step used Blender's native operation after the typed ForgeMCP binding preview exceeded its attribute limit. The user-confirmed backward finger bending remains an open issue. Anatomical correction and webcam capture are proposed future work only.

October 29, 2026 — Blender production skills integrated into Codex

The integration report adds the complete 94-skill Blender Skills pack by Arjun Shukla (@arjun988) to the repository's Codex project skills, with the upstream MIT notice and source commit retained. A ForgeMCP bridge skill maps production guidance to supported typed tools and documents session identity, preview/apply, read-back, persistence, render, export, and visual evidence boundaries. Codex now lists the project-local skills. This is a prompt and documentation integration only: no Blender adapter or MCP implementation changed, and no additional runtime capability is claimed.

October 26, 2026 — Epic UE 5.6.1 source repository access blocked

The Epic source repository investigation attempted the official EpicGames/UnrealEngine repository and the exact 5.6.1-release Engine/Build/Build.version through the configured GitHub connection. Both requests returned 404, so the tag SHA and tag contents are UNKNOWN pending repository authorization. Epic's access requirements are documented in the report. No clone, mirror, download, engine setup, build, or project mutation was attempted. Read-only inspection of the installed engine source confirms UE 5.6.1 changelist 44394996 and extends the capability map across PCG, Chaos, AI, Control Rig, MetaSounds, Editor scripting, and other source modules. Client catalog parity and Blueprint runner/Niagara validation remain the immediate ForgeMCP priorities.

October 26, 2026 — Unreal Engine source integration preparation

The Unreal Engine Source Integration Preparation report verifies the active ForgeMCPDev Editor against the installed UE 5.6.1 source at [local path]

October 26, 2026 — Universal Unreal control architecture audit

The universal control architecture and capability roadmap includes the foundation-operation design requested in option 2. Read-only audit confirmed the authenticated ForgeMCPDev / UE 5.6.1 session, 131 source-declared MCP tools versus 128 currently exposed by the connected client, and the missing Blueprint test-runner trio. It inventories current Unreal coverage and gaps, proposes a versioned capability registry and shared discover/inspect/preview/apply/compile/save/reload/runtime workflow, and sequences the universal roadmap. No source, test, build, Editor, or asset changes were made; pre-existing Git changes were preserved. Trello's ForgeMCP project status card was updated with this audit and next priorities.

October 26, 2026 — Native large-graph pass; runner response and Niagara gates remain blocked

The runner and Niagara validation report records the current ForgeMCPDev session [session id redacted] on UE 5.6.1, PIE stopped, and the temporary -DisablePlugins=Fab launch workaround. The large-graph native test later wrote an explicit PASS for 1,001 nodes, but its 12.23-second synchronous start exceeded the MCP response deadline, so the caller did not receive a run handle. An earlier run failed because automation mode ended; the trigger remains unknown. The scoped primitive journal test passed through preview/start/status.

Niagara component-template assignment and generic Blueprint save/reload remain unsupported; Niagara fixture tests and PIE were NOT EXECUTED. No source code or ViperBP assets changed in this validation. ForgeMCP/Viper production readiness remains BLOCKED. Next: fix and verify bounded runner orchestration and expose its commands to the current client, then implement disposable Niagara template and persistence acceptance.

October 26, 2026 — Inspection passed; journal build passed, startup acceptance blocked

Latest progress and acceptance matrix records the current evidence boundary. The owning Codex MCP connection and exact ForgeMCPDev identity were verified after the project-folder move. One explicitly approved normal close, binary backup, full build and reopen completed on UE 5.6.1.

Gate Latest recorded result
Native inspection build and activation PASS. Full ForgeMCPDevEditor target completed; ten original binary files were backed up with verified SHA-256 hashes. Inspection commands and a native capabilities call succeeded after reopen.
Native large-graph inspection PASS. ForgeMCP.BlueprintInspection.LargeGraphPaginationAndTrace: transient 1,001-node fixture, 1 succeeded, zero errors and zero warnings. This is not saved/reloaded fixture acceptance.
Scoped journal source validation PASS at source gates. Python lint and 568 tests; all four affected C++ translation units compile against UE 5.6.1 without linking or replacing the loaded DLL.
Later scoped journal full build/link PASS. After owner approval, ten current binary files were backed up and the full Editor target completed 37 actions. The same project was reopened once.
Latest Editor startup and queued native tests BLOCKED. TedsOutliner requested unloaded LevelEditor during startup. The Editor exited before an authenticated session or automation report; both queued tests were NOT RUN. No connected Editor remains.
Scoped journal native behavior and client exposure UNVERIFIED. Real compiler-failure, rollback/refusal and fixture assertions have not run. The two new patch wrappers are not exposed in the owning client.
Full Blueprint infrastructure and production INCOMPLETE. Structural authoring, own/inherited Niagara defaults, generic functions/runtime behavior, explicit save, independent reload and complete fixture/regression acceptance remain open. ViperBP is untouched and NO-GO.

The inspection implementation report retains the original audit and superseded activation blocker. The activation evidence records its later resolution. The scoped journal source report covers typed move/default/explicit-link operations, targeted journals, separate package backups and guarded restoration, with runtime acceptance explicitly pending.

Latest result and next dependency: the additional activation was explicitly approved and attempted. The startup failure report records the successful build and failed reopen. Native work stopped at that acceptance gate; read-only startup diagnosis is next. No additional launch, binary restoration, engine patch or asset recovery was attempted. Landscape independent reload, visual/collision and Phase 6C release gaps remain separate and open.

October 24, 2026

Expanded and organized the ForgeMCP Encyclopedia to preserve development chronology, successful milestones, failed experiments, and recovery operations. Historical records retain their original titles and dates; filename dates are discovery hints, not independently verified event times.

  • Development chronology
  • Recovery checkpoint inventory
  • Terrain acceptance audit: recorded live checks passed; independent reload and close-up visual acceptance remained blocked.
  • Stage 2E reload attempt: preserve the blocked outcome.
  • Connection recovery and consolidation [not indexed]: bounded historical results do not establish current client persistence.

October 24 publication verification (historical)

Python lint passed (ruff check server tests); Python tests passed (562 tests). These checks do not establish a current native plugin compile, live Editor behavior, or owning-client tool exposure. No Editor was contacted or rebuilt for this source-control cleanup.

Plugin source, MCP host, tests, and documentation are published. Unreal Engine installations, project assets, raw recovery-project copies, runtime registrations, local configuration backups, and Git backup bundles remain local. Large evidence catalogs use Git LFS.

Adding future updates

Add the newest dated entry first. Give each entry an ISO event date when known, a descriptive title, evidence links, development status, and separate source, automated-test, native-build, live-runtime, and saved/reloaded results. Use Unknown when evidence is missing. Preserve superseded and failed records and explain which later evidence supersedes them.
